text:
Hello everybody, I am working on the p2sh tx documentation chapter (& slicing prev chap into smaller ones). 

I don't quite understand the `active_forks` argument in `script.to_string(active_forks)`. It seems this argument is the same as the block version miner signaling for softforks, but as far as I can tell, only affects "nop2->CLTV" or "nop3->CSV" in the returned string. So to get CLTV or CSV as the string output, I have to explicitly input the `uin32_t active_fork` argument with the respective bit activated.

Q: Why only specifically these 2 cases, and only for the tx `script.to_string` method? 

Thanks in advance!!

elements.text: Because these are the only opcodes that change behavior as the result of supported forks. The arguments is not the block version number, it’s the set of active forks.

text: Because these are the only opcodes that change behavior as the result of supported forks. The arguments is not the block version number, it’s the set of active forks.

elements.text: The reason they apply to that method is because the textual serialization will change based on what forks are presumed active. This serialization is generally for human consumption.

elements.text: Scripts consist only of opcodes 0-255. Some opcodes have associated data. When you create an operation from data the data opcode is determined for you. Given that there are potentially multiple choices of data opcode (based on length) it will chose the "minimal" (shortest mapping) opcode. The other convention is to use the "nominal" (simpler mapping) data opcode. You'll see both terms in the comments and parameter names. The construction you are using is:
operation(data_chunk&& uncoded, bool minimal=true)
